title: HB373 (132st Legislature (2017-2018)): Permit concealed carry in courthouses and govt buildings

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Ohio) (gun-policy Stage 5, Ohio); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Ohio text (As Introduced (00_IN), ; official copy, https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_132/legislation/hb373/00_IN/pdf/ (Open States text id 90121701))
provenance.note: As introduced (132nd GA); no later amendments in the text read. The (6) item in R.C. 2923.126 is rebuilt from text mixing struck and added words (it ends ';.' as printed). Struck: the ban on licensee carry into a courthouse or building with a courtroom (R.C. 2923.126(B)(3), list renumbered); 'this state or' in the government-facility ban and definitions, so state buildings are no longer barred; the handgun-handover condition in R.C. 2923.123(C); the firearm-in-vehicle rules for the capitol garage (R.C. 105.41(N)) and Riffe center garage (R.C. 123.011(B)). Courthouse limits by court rule stay in R.C. 2923.123.

operative_text:
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.126): (6) Any building that is a government facility of a political subdivision of this state and that is not a building that is used primarily as a shelter, restroom, parking facility for motor vehicles, or rest facility if the governing body with authority over the building has enacted an ordinance, or policy that prohibits a licensee from carrying a concealed handgun into the building;. (7) A place in which federal law prohibits the carrying of handguns.
